chunks: And among what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man who has an ulcer or a wound and is unable to bandage it or wash its blood. He said: He should perform salat (prayer), and he should not wash his garment every day except once, for he is not able to wash his garment every hour.

So this report as well is to be understood as referring to recommendation, and we have fully covered what relates to this chapter in our larger book. Whoever wants it may examine it there, if Allah wills.

key_terms.الْجُرْحُ: a wound from which blood may continue to flow
key_terms.الْقَرْحُ: an ulcer or sore producing ongoing impurity
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment affected by the blood
key_terms.مَرَّةً: once, indicating the limited frequency of washing
key_terms.يُصَلِّي: he should perform salat (prayer) despite the hardship

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for praying with blood on one’s clothing when a wound cannot be constantly washed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for a person whose wound or ulcer continuously produces blood and who cannot keep washing or binding it. He is instructed to continue salat (prayer), and to wash his garment only once daily, reflecting legal ease in cases of hardship. The compiler then states that this report is understood as indicating recommendation.
